We have a time-sensitive pilot with MedScribe (starts June 1). They want a committed slice with a predictable headroom policy and a written fallback matrix in case we hit a regional saturation event. Sales asked for two things before the procurement signature:

1) an ops-level fallback matrix (what model variants we downgrade to, latency impact estimates, and token-cost delta)
2) a short procurement-friendly MOP (how we notify, expected SLAs during fallback, and billing adjustments)

I started a draft (attached: medscribe_fallback_matrix_v1.xlsx and pilot_capacity_mop.pdf). Can product/ops review and confirm policy boundaries? Specific asks:
- Kimberly: confirm permitted downgrade families and any quality gating we must preserve (e.g., early stopping, quantization floor)
- Laura: confirm alerting/playbooks and add on-call contact + DocuSign timeline for emergency carveouts
- Marcus: feasibility check — can we guarantee burst capacity in us-west for the first 2 weeks of pilot, or do we need to route to us-central as primary fallback?

Neha, once we have the above, I’ll draft the procurement note for MedScribe procurement/legal.

Thanks,

Confirming receipt and quick infra read:

- Us-west reserved pool currently has capacity to cover the initial committed slice (8 GPUs) plus a short burst (2 GPUs) for the first 10 days. After that we’re at risk of contention with other enterprise pilots scheduled in week 3.
- We can pre-provision a warm fallback in us-central (same instance types) but cross-region KV cache warmup will add ~30–45s cold-start for first few requests per session. That’s acceptable for batch workflows but not for low-latency interactive sessions.
- Kernel availability: all optimized kernels are present for the rwd-xl/l/m families on the us-west hardware. Quantized 8-bit rwd-l has been smoke-tested; 4-bit has not.

Action items for me: add a short infra note in the MOP on expected cold-start windows and a recommended throttle policy. I’ll attach the infra note to the runbook.
